mrts.address: 14741 Wolf Mountain Road, Grass Valley, CA 95949
mrts.hours: Wednesday - Sunday, 8:00 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. (closed Monday and Tuesday and on major holidays)

mrts-hhw.name: Household Hazardous Waste area, McCourtney Road Transfer Station (free for residents)
mrts-hhw.address: 14741 Wolf Mountain Road, Grass Valley, CA 95949
mrts-hhw.note: State law limits one trip to 15 gallons or 125 pounds; carry it in spill- and leak-proof containers.

battery-drop-off.name: Household battery drop-off (or a Ziploc bag on top of your blue recycling cart on pickup day)
battery-drop-off.address: Briar Patch Community Market (290 Sierra College, Grass Valley); Nevada County Government Center (950 Maidu Ave, Nevada City); Grass Valley Library (207 Mill St); McCourtney Road Transfer Station; Madelyn Helling Library (980 Helling Way, Nevada City); Nevada City City Hall (317 Broad St); North San Juan and Washington Transfer Stations

grocery-store.name: Plastic bag collection at a grocery store
grocery-store.address: Many grocery stores in Nevada County take plastic shopping bags.

rules.how: Empty it. Put it loose in the blue recycling cart. Bottles with a CRV label can also go to a buyback center for the refund.
rules.quote: Empty glass jars and bottles

rules.how: Empty it. Put it loose in the blue recycling cart. Cans with a CRV label can also go to a buyback center for the refund.
rules.quote: Empty aluminum and metal cans

rules.item: plastic bottle, jug, jar or container
rules.how: Empty it. Put it loose in the blue recycling cart.
rules.quote: Empty plastic bottles, jugs, jars, and containers

rules.how: Flatten it, keep it dry, put it in the blue recycling cart. A greasy pizza box goes in the green cart instead.
rules.quote: Flattened cardboard, and clean and dry paper

rules.how: Keep it clean and dry. Put it loose in the blue recycling cart.
rules.quote: Flattened cardboard, and clean and dry paper

rules.how: Empty it. Put it in the blue recycling cart.
rules.quote: Empty paper and plastic to-go cups (coffee cups and soda cups)

rules.how: Not in the recycling cart, and never bag your recyclables. Take clean plastic bags to a grocery store collection bin.
rules.quote: Bags are not acceptable in your recycling cart. Please keep recyclables loose. Do not place recyclables in clear bags. Plastic shopping bags are accepted at many grocery stores in Nevada County, where you may recycle these safely.

rules.how: Green organics cart. No plastic or compostable bag liners.
rules.quote: Nevada County residents are now asked to place their food scraps and food-soiled paper in their existing or newly delivered green cart.

rules.item: greasy pizza box or food-soiled cardboard
rules.how: Green organics cart.
rules.quote: Soiled cardboard, including pizza boxes, can go in the organics cart, too.

rules.how: Green organics cart (non-shiny paper plates too).
rules.quote: Food waste is spoiled food, vegetable scraps, egg shells, coffee grounds, coffee filters, tea bags, cooked meat and bones, diary, paper towels, paper napkins, non-shiny paper plates, real wine corks, pet hair and pizza boxes.

rules.how: Green organics cart; the lid must close. Big loads can go to McCourtney Road Transfer Station.
rules.quote: Place food waste, food-soiled paper, grass clippings, flowers and leaves, wood branches & untreated lumber in your yard waste cart.

rules.item: blackberry vines, Scotch broom or palm fronds
rules.how: Not in the green cart. The sources do not say where they go: call WM.
rules.quote: No invasive plants such as blackberry vines, scotch bloom or palm leaves.

rules.how: Trash cart. The county compost takes 60 days; these bags take longer.
rules.quote: These bags can be put in the regular trash and they will break down in the landfill.

rules.how: Wait until it is cold, bag it, then trash cart.
rules.quote: Wait until it cools, bag, then place in the trash.

rules.how: Trash cart. Never the green cart.
rules.quote: No trash, plastic, glass, metal, treated wood, hazardous waste, diapers or pet waste.

rules.how: Never in any cart. Put them in a Ziploc bag on top of the blue cart on recycling day, or take them to a drop-off.
rules.quote: Residents who have curbside WM service can place these type of batteries in a Ziploc bag and put it on top of their blue recycle cart on their regular recycle pickup day.

rules.item: car, lawnmower or power tool battery
rules.how: Take it to McCourtney Road Transfer Station.
rules.quote: Larger batteries include: auto batteries, power tool batteries, lawnmower batteries, and more.

rules.item: device with a built-in battery (vape, earbuds, power bank)
rules.how: Do not remove the battery. Take the whole device to McCourtney Road Transfer Station.
rules.quote: No need to remove the battery, just take the entire device to:

rules.how: Free at McCourtney Road Transfer Station (Staples in Grass Valley takes some items). Wipe your data first.
rules.quote: There is no charge to drop off e-waste.

rules.how: Free in the metal section at McCourtney Road Transfer Station.
rules.quote: These need to be taken to the metal section of the McCourtney Road Transfer Station. There is no fee to drop off small appliances here.

rules.how: McCourtney Road Transfer Station; pay the fee at the scale house first.
rules.quote: Appliances must be paid for at the transfer station’s scale house before dropping off.

rules.how: McCourtney Road Transfer Station metal section; pieces no longer than 4 feet; no cylinders.
rules.quote: All metals are accepted, however, no metal cylinders of any type, nor solar panels.

rules.how: Free at the Household Hazardous Waste area at McCourtney Road Transfer Station.
rules.quote: Mercury Products such as fluorescent tubes and bulbs, mercury gauges, electrical switches/relays, pilot light sensor/thermostats

rules.how: Never in the trash (state rule). Local pages do not name a drop-off for LEDs: call WM.
rules.quote: Never put LED lights in the trash because they often have toxic metals.

rules.how: Free at the Household Hazardous Waste area. Never in any cart or down the drain.
rules.quote: It is illegal to dispose of household hazardous waste in the trash, down the drain or by abandonment

rules.how: Free at the Household Hazardous Waste area. For motor oil WM also gives you a curbside jug (call 530-274-3090).
rules.quote: Oil and oil filter Recycling

rules.how: Household Hazardous Waste area. Do not put cans labeled TOXIC or FLAMMABLE in the trash.
rules.quote: Nonempty aerosol cans that contain hazardous materials

rules.how: Sharps collection at the Household Hazardous Waste area. Use a sealed sharps container.
rules.quote: Sharps Collection, which includes needles and lancets. Medication is not accepted

rules.how: The transfer station does not take medication. Call WM.
rules.quote: Sharps Collection, which includes needles and lancets. Medication is not accepted

rules.how: McCourtney Road Transfer Station: free under 5 gallons, $14.37 for 5 to 25 gallons. Never in a cart.
rules.quote: Less than 5 gallons FREE

rules.how: Free at McCourtney Road Transfer Station if dry and clean, up to five per resident.
rules.quote: Non-soiled mattresses are free to drop off, up to five per resident.

rules.how: Separate carpet from padding and roll it up. No area rugs or scraps.
rules.quote: Carpet and padding recycling program is now found at the McCourtney Road Transfer Station.

rules.how: McCourtney Road Transfer Station; the fee depends on size and whether it is on the rim.
rules.quote: Tires can be disposed of at the McCourtney Road Transfer Station during operation hours.

rules.how: Treated wood receiving area at McCourtney Road Transfer Station; 4 feet or shorter.
rules.quote: These materials are considered hazardous waste and are accepted in the treated wood receiving area at the transfer station.

rules.how: Not accepted at McCourtney Road. Take it to Recology in Auburn (or offer a working panel for reuse).
rules.quote: Solar panels can be taken to Recology, 12305 Shale Ridge Road, Auburn CA 95602.

rules.how: Not in any cart and not accepted as drop-off loads. Call WM to schedule a dumpster.
rules.quote: Rocks, Dirt and Concrete Call 530-274-3090 to schedule a dumpster.

rules.how: Prohibited at the transfer station and never in a cart. Call WM.
rules.quote: Ammunition, guns, or explosives

unresolved.why: Common items that a generic alias would mis-match, and that the local pages read on 2026-11-24 do not settle. They always answer 'ask', never a guessed cart.
